sonnet.problem: Card 3 already told the baker the date is twilight on the fourteenth day. Card 12's right answer, 'Twilight on the fourteenth day', is that same fact asked again. The wrong answers (sunrise on the first day, noon on the tenth day) are easy to rule out from card 3, so the baker doesn't have to reason anything new.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The story card asks 'Does he need a special pass, a different rulebook, a cousin on the inside?' Its rhetorical questions point to 'no'. That rules out the False answer on card 20 (same statute for foreigner and native) before the baker answers.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
